verses.gurmukhi: ਫਲ ਦੇ ਵਟ ਵਗਾਇਆ ਤਛਣਹਾਰੈ ਤਾਰਿ ਤਰੰਦਾ।
verses.translit_en: fal dhe vaT vagaiaa tachhanahaarai taar tara(n)dhaa|

en.bdb: A tree gives fruits to stone thrower and wooden boat to the cutter to get him across.

verses.gurmukhi: ਤਛੇ ਪੁਤ ਨ ਡੋਬਈ ਪੁਤ ਵੈਰੁ ਜਲ ਜੀ ਨ ਧਰੰਦਾ।
verses.translit_en: tachhe put na ddobiee put vair jal jee na dhara(n)dhaa|

en.bdb: Water, the father (of tree) not remembering the evil deeds (of carpenter) does not drown the boat along with carpenter.

verses.gurmukhi: ਵਰਸੈ ਹੋਇ ਸਹੰਸ ਧਾਰ ਮਿਲਿ ਗਿਲ ਜਲੁ ਨੀਵਾਣਿ ਚਲੰਦਾ।
verses.translit_en: varasai hoi saha(n)s dhaar mil gil jal neevaan chala(n)dhaa|

en.bdb: Becoming thousands of currents when it rains, water in thousand streams flows towards the lower places.

verses.gurmukhi: ਡੋਬੈ ਡਬੈ ਅਗਰ ਨੋ ਆਪੁ ਛਡਿ ਪੁਤ ਪੈਜ ਰਖੰਦਾ।
verses.translit_en: ddobai ddabai agar no aap chhadd put paij rakha(n)dhaa|

en.bdb: Wood of agar tree is drowned but repudiating ego, water saves the honour of its son, wood of the tree [in fact agar(eaglewood) floats under water surface].

verses.gurmukhi: ਤਰਿ ਡੁਬੈ ਡੁਬਾ ਤਰੈ ਜਿਣਿ ਹਾਰੈ ਹਾਰੈ ਸੁ ਜਿਣੰਦਾ।
verses.translit_en: tar ddubai ddubaa tarai jin haarai haarai su jina(n)dhaa|

en.bdb: He who goes on swimming upon the water (of love) may be understood as drowned and he who drowns in love, may be considered as having swum across.

verses.gurmukhi: ਉਲਟਾ ਖੇਲੁ ਪਿਰੰਮ ਦਾ ਪੈਰਾਂ ਉਪਰਿ ਸੀਸੁ ਨਿਵੰਦਾ।
verses.translit_en: aulaTaa khel pira(n)m dhaa pairaa(n) upar sees niva(n)dhaa|

en.bdb: Similarly, winner in the world loses and becoming detached and the loser, one wins (ultimately).
Inverse is the tradition of love which makes the head bow to the feet. The altruist Sikh considers none as the bad or the worse.
